findings.body:
Removing the `ALLOWED_HOSTS` check means `deliver()` will POST to any caller-supplied `url` via `urllib.request.urlopen`. A customer- or attacker-controlled endpoint can target cloud metadata (`http://169.254.169.254/`), loopback, or internal hosts, and `urllib` will follow redirects off-allowlist by default.

Restore an egress policy before merge: HTTPS-only, resolve and pin IPs blocking private/link-local/metadata ranges (and DNS rebinding), and/or a configurable per-tenant host allowlist. Keep the check immediately before `urlopen`, and disable redirect following to a different host.

summary:
## Verdict

This change opens a **server-side request forgery (SSRF)** hole by deleting the only host allowlist before `urlopen`. Do not merge until outbound webhook URLs are constrained again.

## What went wrong

`deliver()` previously resolved the URL hostname and rejected anything outside `ALLOWED_HOSTS`. That guard is gone; the function now POSTs to whatever string is passed as `url`. Anyone who can set a customer webhook URL (or influence `event` delivery config) can point the runner at link-local metadata (`169.254.169.254`), loopback, internal RFC1918 hosts, or non-HTTP schemes `urllib` will still open.

Supporting enterprise customer endpoints is a valid product goal, but it requires an explicit egress policy (HTTPS-only, DNS rebinding-safe IP checks, block private/link-local/metadata ranges, and/or a per-tenant allowlist), not an unconditional `urlopen`.

## Notes

- Pre-existing: `json_dumps` is referenced but not defined/imported in this file; unrelated to this diff but will break the call path once host checks are restored.
- No other files in the repo compensate for the removed check.

**Recommendation:** request-changes

verification.reason: The patch removes ALLOWED_HOSTS and the hostname check that previously rejected non-allowlisted URLs; deliver() now urlopen()s any caller-supplied url with no egress controls, enabling SSRF to metadata/internal hosts. Critical severity is appropriate for unrestricted server-side request egress.
